title: How many one rupee coins weigh as much as a child?
description: Instead of jaggery, one rupee coins are used to equal the weight of a child. We assume the weights, change both to grams, and divide to estimate the number of coins. Keeko doubts dividing kilograms by grams directly.
teaching_notes: One idea: to find how many small things make up a big weight, put both weights in the same unit and divide. Watch for students who divide kilograms by grams directly.

source: About how many 1-rupee coins weigh as much as Roxie
video_script.why: A count of small things is the big weight divided by the small weight, with both in the same unit.
video_script.substitution: Change the child's weight to grams, then divide it by the weight of one coin.
video_script.anchor: one rupee coins that weigh as much as a child
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko divides 45 kg by 4 g and gets about 11. Kilograms and grams are different units; 45 kg is 45000 g, and 45000 divided by 4 is far larger.
video_script.payoff_line: Make both weights the same unit, then divide

final_answer.spoken: About eleven thousand two hundred fifty coins are needed. That is roughly eleven thousand coins.

names.Ruhee: the child whose weight the one rupee coins must equal

maths_rules: number of coins = weight of the child ÷ weight of one coin
assume 45 kg and a coin of about 4 g
the slip: 45 ÷ 4 mixes kg with g
video_script.design: A balance carries the child on one pan and coins on the other. The two weights are written in the same unit before the division is built.
open_questions: The coin weight of about 4 g is the worklist's assumption; the book suggests measuring a coin.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, divide the weight of the child by the weight of one coin.
<bookmark mark='assume'/>Assume forty five kilograms for the child, and about four grams for a coin.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, put both weights in grams.
<bookmark mark='grams'/>One kilogram is one thousand grams, so forty five kilograms is forty five thousand grams.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, divide forty five thousand by four.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split it into forty thousand and five thousand.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Forty thousand divided by four is ten thousand. Five thousand divided by four is one thousand two hundred fifty.

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, check by multiplying back.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Ten thousand coins weigh forty thousand grams, and one thousand two hundred fifty coins weigh five thousand grams.
Together that is forty five thousand grams.
